338	#### 8. Flags
339	
340	Our own SVGs, one standalone component per flag under `frontend/src/app/shared/flags/`, written by
341	hand from the published constructions (no library): Colombia 2:3, three horizontal bands 2:1:1
342	yellow/blue/red; Chile 2:3, two equal bands white over red, a blue square canton the height of the
343	white band, a white five-pointed star centred in the canton on a circle whose diameter is half the
344	canton side (Wikipedia, "Flag of Colombia" and "Flag of Chile", read 2026-11-21; neither law fixes
345	exact colours, so the colour values are the published approximations, ADR-0011). Each is `viewBox`
346	geometry only (`rect`, one `polygon`), fills from component tokens through CSS classes (no hex in
347	templates), `aria-hidden="true"`, `focusable="false"`, no `<title>`, no text; under 1 kB of
348	template each. A 1 px `--color-border-control` ring (4.23:1 on the header) separates the dark blue
349	areas from the near-black background. Where the flags appear and what replaces them for other
350	countries: ADR-0011.
351	
352	### Consequences
353	
354	- Good, because every value has one home and one name; the guard makes "no loose values" a gate
355	  failure, not a review comment (D1), at zero dependency cost (D8).
356	- Good, because the contrast proof is a test over the real token file: a tuned colour that breaks a
357	  pair fails the gate, gradients included (D2).
358	- Good, because the semantic tier isolates components from raw values: a light theme or a palette
359	  change touches `tokens.css` only.
360	- Good, because the icon package is the maintained one, compatible with Angular 22.3.0, hides
361	  icons by default and has no `innerHTML` path (D5, D6); the transfer cost of 22 icons is about
362	  4 kB.
363	- Good, because both fonts are OFL-1.1, same-origin, and the text face is chosen for the exact
364	  data the form collects.
365	- Bad, because a regex-based CSS guard is weaker than a real parser: a construct it does not
366	  anticipate (a value split across lines, an escape) could slip through — mitigation: the style
367	  files are small and simple; the sensitivity self-test covers each rule; the code-reviewer still
368	  reads the CSS; A2 remains the upgrade path.
369	- Bad, because `@lucide/angular` costs about 3.2 kB **raw** per icon (each icon is a component), so
370	  the raw initial size grows faster than the transfer size — mitigation: icons used only on step 1
371	  move to the lazy chunk (ADR-0012); budgets are measured on every build.
372	- Bad, because the Archivo width-axis file is 90 kB, about 55 kB more than its weight-only file
373	  (`archivo-latin-wght-normal.woff2`, 34,928 bytes) — mitigation: not preloaded, `swap`, used only
374	  for headings and prices, cached after the first visit; if HC2 prefers bytes over the width
375	  treatment, switching to the weight-only file is a one-line change.
376	- Bad, because a 3:1 border on every interactive card and input is heavier than the "thin, subtle"
377	  borders of the reference — mitigation: 1 px width, and subtle hairlines stay on non-interactive
378	  panels only (*Spec impact* 2).
379	- Neutral: the dark-only theme means users with a light-mode preference get the dark UI; that is
380	  the brief.
381	
382	### Strongest argument against
383	
384	Stylelint (A2) is the standard tool for exactly this rule: it parses CSS with PostCSS, reports
385	the line and column in the editor while the developer types, has a maintained
386	`declaration-strict-value` plugin, and `stylelint-config-standard` would catch a whole class of
387	other CSS mistakes for free. A home-made regex guard re-implements a parser badly, will drift as
388	the CSS grows, and gives feedback only when the test suite runs. Adding two pinned, MIT-licensed
389	devDependencies is a small price for that.
390	
391	**Why we accept it:** the rule set here is narrow and project-specific (tier prefixes, "no
392	primitive in components", breakpoints that must equal token values, a single declaring file), so
393	Stylelint would need custom rules or plugin configuration for most of it anyway, plus a lint-step
394	change. The repository already enforces ADR rules as Vitest static guards that run in the gate
395	(ADR-0008, ADR-0009), and the sensitivity self-test makes a silent pass visible. If the guard
396	proves brittle during implementation or review, A2 is a contained switch: add the two
397	devDependencies through a superseding note and delete the guard.

content.content: 20 ADRs are not rewritten: ADR-0001 stays as it is, and this ADR states the exception. 21 22 ## Decision Drivers 23 24 - D1. Adding a country stays content-only: a new published `country` must work with no front-end 25 change, with sensible visuals (ADR-0001 D3; US-04-AC-03 second scenario). 26 - D2. The Strapi contract, seed, permissions and proxy do not change (story, "Rules that do not 27 change"; US-04-BR-07; ADR-0002). 28 - D3. AA contrast of the accent on the dark surfaces is proven by test (US-04-BR-02, AC-02). 29 - D4. The flag is decorative next to the country name, never the only indicator; the country name 30 still comes from Strapi (US-04-BR-03). 31 - D5. No `innerHTML`, no third-party runtime origin, no uploaded SVG rendered as markup 32 (ADR-0009, ADR-0002; spec §9). 33 - D6. The exception to ADR-0001 is as narrow as possible and checked mechanically (CLAUDE.md §9). 34 35 ## Considered Options 36 37 1. **A. Presentation-only country-visuals map in the front end**, keyed by ISO code, with a neutral 38 fallback (globe icon, brand accent) for any other published country. 39 2. **B. Extend the Strapi `country` type** with an accent colour (validated hex) and a flag asset. 40 3. **C. Derive visuals from the code at runtime**: the flag emoji built from the ISO code's regional 41 indicator symbols, and no per-country accent. 42 43 ## Decision Outcome 44 45 Chosen option: **"A. 399	### Confirmation
400	
401	- `static-guards` / `design-guards` (US-04-AC-01, AC-19, AC-21): the rules of §2; at most two
402	  `@font-face` families, both WOFF2 with `font-display: swap`, `src` same-origin (`/fonts/…`);
403	  `frontend/package.json` versions exact and the dependency names equal the pre-US-04 list plus
404	  exactly `@lucide/angular`, `@fontsource-variable/archivo`,
405	  `@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next`, and the additions of ADR-0012.
406	- `contrast.spec.ts` (US-04-AC-02): a pure WCAG ratio function with known reference values
407	  (black/white 21, `#777777` on white about 4.48), and every row of `contrast-pairs.json` resolved
408	  from `tokens.css`.
409	- `field-icons.spec.ts` (US-04-AC-04): every key of §7 maps to its icon; an unknown key of each
410	  non-checkbox type gets the default; `checkbox` gets none.
411	- Component tests (AC-04, AC-20): every `svg` in the wizard is `aria-hidden="true"`; accessible
412	  names and `textContent` of the buttons of AC-04 unchanged.
413	- HC3 visual review (AC-23): the look matches §4–§8.
414	
415	## Pros and Cons of the Options
416	
417	### A1. Static guard in Vitest (chosen)
418	
419	- Good, because it runs in the existing gate with no new dependency and follows the repository's
420	  pattern for ADR rules (`static-guards.spec.ts`).
421	- Good, because project-specific rules (tiers, breakpoints equal to tokens, single declaring file)
422	  are a few lines each.
423	- Bad, because it is regex-based (no CSS parser) and reports only at test time.
424	
425	### A2. Stylelint 18.1.0 + `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` 1.13.0
426	
427	Verified on npm (2026-11-21): `stylelint@18.1.0` MIT, 19 direct dependencies;
428	`stylelint-declaration-strict-value@1.13.0` MIT, peer `stylelint >=16 <=18`.
429	
430	- Good, because it is a real parser with editor feedback and a large rule ecosystem.
431	- Bad, because the tier, breakpoint and single-file rules still need custom configuration or a
432	  plugin; two more devDependencies (with their transitive tree) and a lint-step change.
433	
434	### B1. Dark only (chosen)
435	
436	- Good, because it is the brief, halves the contrast rows and the screenshot set.
437	- Bad, because there is no light alternative for people who prefer one.
438	
439	### B2. Dark and light by `prefers-color-scheme`
440	
441	- Good, because it respects the system preference.
442	- Bad, because every AC-02 row and every AC-22 screenshot doubles, and the brief describes only the
443	  dark look; the light palette would be invented, not briefed.
444	
445	### C1. `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0 (chosen)
446	
447	- Good, because it is the Lucide team's current Angular package (the README links a migration guide
448	  from `lucide-angular`), standalone and signal-based, compatible with 22.3.0, ISC.
449	- Good, because rendering uses template bindings only and icons are hidden by default.
450	- Bad, because each icon is a compiled component: +78.24 kB raw for 22 icons (measured).
451	
452	### C2. `@ng-icons/core` 36.1.0 + `@ng-icons/lucide` 36.1.0
453	
454	Verified: `@ng-icons/core` MIT, peer `@angular/core >=22.0.0`; `@ng-icons/lucide` ISC.
455	
456	- Good, because one generic component and SVG strings make it small: +13.27 kB raw / +2.50 kB
457	  transfer for the same 22 icons (measured).
458	- Bad, because it inserts the SVG string with `innerHTML` (`fesm2022/ng-icons-core.mjs:458`, `:486`)
459	  inside the library. Our guard would not see it, but it is the exact path ADR-0009 and spec §9
460	  rule out for icons.
461	- Bad, because icons are registered and referenced by string name (`name="lucideIdCard"`), so a typo

9	# ADR-0012: Accessible custom select and date picker on `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, bound to Signal Forms (amends ADR-0004)
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	US-04 replaces the browser's `<select>` and `<input type="date">` of step 1 with design-system
14	controls: a select with an icon, search for long lists and the selected option marked, and a date
15	field that accepts typed dd/mm/aaaa and opens a calendar with month and year navigation and days
16	disabled by the `minAge` rule (US-04-BR-05, BR-06). The story requires them to be "built on
17	accessible primitives, not from scratch: Angular CDK (Overlay, Listbox, a11y) or `@angular/aria`
18	if it is stable in our version", with the WAI-ARIA combobox/listbox and date picker dialog
19	patterns, a bottom sheet on mobile, and validations and stored values unchanged. ADR-0004
20	(Accepted) chose Signal Forms with **native controls** (its driver D7) and its implementation note
21	makes `syncNative` the only writer of number and date keys, built on `validity.badInput`. This ADR
22	picks the primitives, defines how the controls plug into Signal Forms and the shared validation
23	core, and amends ADR-0004 where it assumed native controls (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11..Q-13).
24	
25	## Decision Drivers
26	
27	- D1. WAI-ARIA APG patterns: combobox with listbox popup (select-only and list autocomplete), date
28	  picker dialog; full keyboard map of US-04-AC-06, AC-09; focus trapped and returned; polite
29	  announcements (story; US-04-BR-05, BR-06, BR-13).
30	- D2. Built on primitives, not from scratch; exact versions, permissive licence; `@angular/cdk`
31	  equal to the framework version (story; US-04-BR-14; CLAUDE.md §4).
32	- D3. Same validation, same stored values, same error timing and focus target as before
33	  (US-04-BR-07, AC-11; ADR-0004: string editing model, `validateField` as the only rule engine,
34	  `touched && invalid`, `focusBoundControl()` on a failed submit; ADR-0003 stored shape).
35	- D4. The labelled, focused element is an `<input>` or `<button>` targeted by the field's
36	  `<label for>`, so `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the existing `aria-*` bindings keep working
37	  (US-04-BR-05, Q-04 constraint, Q-06, §11.1).
38	- D5. Typed date dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of the browser locale, stored as ISO;
39	  unreadable text behaves like the former `badInput` (US-04-BR-06, Q-05; US-01-BR-01, AC-09 note).
40	- D6. Disabled days come from the same pure validator, no second implementation (US-04-BR-06).
41	- D7. Panels: popover on wide screens, bottom sheet below 600 px; 44 × 44 px targets; no horizontal
42	  scroll (US-04-BR-11, AC-12, Q-13).
43	- D8. Bundle budgets (`angular.json`: initial 500 kB warning) kept or justified (spec §9).
44	- D9. Testable in jsdom component tests and Playwright e2e by role and label, never by class
45	  (story; spec §11.1).
46	
47	## Considered Options
48	
49	1. **A. `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 for the combobox, listbox and year list, with `@angular/cdk`
50	   22.3.0** for overlay positioning, the calendar dialog (focus trap and return), live
51	   announcements and breakpoints; the calendar grid's date navigation as a pure function.
52	2. **B. `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0 only**: Overlay, `ActiveDescendantKeyManager` (and `cdk/listbox` for
53	   the year list), `Dialog`, `LiveAnnouncer`; the combobox roles, states and key handling wired by
54	   hand around the key manager.
55	3. **C. Angular Material 22.3.0** (`mat-select` / `mat-autocomplete`, `mat-datepicker` with its
56	   multi-year view), restyled to the design system.
57	
58	Building the widgets from scratch is excluded by the story.
59	
60	## Decision Outcome
61	
62	Chosen option: **"A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk`"**, because `@angular/aria` is stable at
63	22.x (the developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0) and implements the APG combobox wiring that
64	option B would have us write by hand (role and states, `aria-activedescendant`, key relay,
65	typeahead, close on focus-out), which is closest to "from scratch" (D1, D2). It works on an
66	`<input>` (editable) and on a `<button>` (select-only), so the labelled element stays a labelable
67	native element (D4). The CDK supplies what `@angular/aria` does not have: overlay positioning with
68	a bottom sheet, a modal dialog with focus trap and return, and the live announcer. Material (C)
69	would bring a complete date picker but a select host that a `<label for>` cannot target and a
70	theming system that competes with our token tiers.
71

95	#### 3. The custom select
96	
97	- **Focus element.** Select-only (fewer than `SEARCH_THRESHOLD` options): a
98	  `<button type="button" ngCombobox>`; `@angular/aria` treats any non-`input`/`textarea` element as
99	  non-editable (`_combobox-chunk.mjs`: `isEditable` checks the tag), so Enter, Space and ArrowDown
100	  open it and printable keys are relayed to the list for typeahead. Searchable (at or above the
101	  threshold): an `<input type="text" ngCombobox>`; typing expands it and writes the filter text.
102	  Either element gets `id="field-<key>"` (input `controlId`), so the existing `<label for>` targets
103	  it. Its accessible name is the label; for the button variant `aria-labelledby` also points at the
104	  label, so the shown value is not folded into the name in any browser.
105	- **Attributes.** `@angular/aria` binds `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`,
106	  `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-controls`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-autocomplete` (packed
107	  `fesm2022/combobox.mjs` host bindings). The form binds `aria-required`, `aria-invalid` and
108	  `aria-describedby` through inputs of `CustomSelect` exactly as today (ADR-0004: bound
109	  explicitly), applied to the focus element.
110	- **List.** `<ul ngComboboxWidget ngListbox>` inside `<ng-template ngComboboxPopup>`, with
111	  `focusMode="activedescendant"`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`; one `ngOption` per
112	  configured option in `sortOrder`, `aria-selected` from the listbox; the selected one shows
113	  `LucideCheck` (hidden) and a style. The prompt "Selecciona una opción" is not an option: it is the
114	  button's text when the value is `''`, and the input's placeholder for a searchable select.
115	- **Behaviour owned by `CustomSelect`** (not provided by `@angular/aria`, each tied to a test row):
116	  Alt+ArrowDown opens on the current option (AC-06); Tab with the list open commits the active
117	  option and lets focus move (AC-06); on a collapsed select-only, a printable key opens and moves to
118	  the first match (AC-06); Escape or leaving a searchable select restores the shown label and clears
119	  the filter without changing the value (AC-07); filtering through `filterOptions()` with the first
120	  match active (Q-11); the result count or the empty text announced politely through the CDK
121	  `LiveAnnouncer` (AC-07, §8.1); a pointer click outside closes without changing the value.
122	- **Panel placement.** A `cdkConnectedOverlay` inside the popup template, anchored to the combobox,
123	  `cdkConnectedOverlayUsePopover="inline"`: in browsers with the Popover API the panel is a native
124	  popover in the top layer, inserted next to the trigger (`@angular/cdk@22.3.0`
125	  `createOverlayRef` defaults `usePopover` to `true` when `showPopover` exists;
126	  `FlexibleOverlayPopoverLocation` `'inline'` inserts it next to the trigger). Below
127	  `--breakpoint-sheet` (`BreakpointObserver` with `(min-width: 37.5em)` false) the same panel uses a
128	  global position strategy anchored to the viewport bottom: full width, at most 85% of the viewport
129	  height, scrollable list, backdrop, option rows of 48 px, and a "Cerrar" button for touch
130	  (`tabindex="-1"`, since focus stays on the combobox and Escape or Tab close it for keyboard users).
131	  Overlays are created with `disableAnimations: true` (ADR-0013).
132	
133	#### 4. The date field and the calendar
134	
135	- **Text box.** `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" id="field-<key>">`, placeholder
136	  "dd/mm/aaaa", hint "Formato: dd/mm/aaaa" first in `aria-describedby`. No input mask.
137	- **Parsing (pure, `date-text.ts`).** `parseDateText(text)` returns `''` for blank text, the ISO
138	  `YYYY-MM-DD` for `d/m/yyyy` with `/`, `-` or `.` separators (1–2 digit day and month) or exactly
139	  8 digits `ddmmyyyy`, and `null` for anything else, including impossible dates (31/04, 29/02 of a
140	  non-leap year) and 2-digit years (Q-05). `formatDateText(iso)` returns `dd/mm/yyyy`. Every AC-08
141	  row is a unit test. The function lives next to the validators and imports nothing from Angular.
142	- **Binding (`transformedValue`).** `DateField` keeps the shown text with Signal Forms'
143	  `transformedValue(value, { parse, format })` (`@publicApi 22.0`, `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
144	  typings). `parse` returns `{ value: iso }`, `{ value: '' }` for blank, and
145	  `{ value: '', error: { kind: 'parse', message: '' } }` for unreadable text, so the stored value
146	  is `''` and the field is invalid through a `parse` error, which Signal Forms reports to the bound
147	  field automatically and which the existing `errorOf()` already maps to the US-01-AC-09 message
148	  rules (no new message). **Verified hazard:** in `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
149	  (`fesm2022/signals.mjs`, `transformedValue`), the raw value is a `linkedSignal(() =>
150	  format(value()))`, so writing `''` to the model would recompute the shown text to `''` and erase
151	  what the person typed (the R1-F03 failure of US-01 in a new form). Therefore `format(iso)` returns
152	  the last typed text whenever that text parses to `iso` (unreadable text parses to `''`), and
153	  `formatDateText(iso)` otherwise. On blur a readable text is normalised to dd/mm/aaaa. A calendar
154	  choice writes the model, and the text follows through `format`. AC-08's empty-`stored` rows prove
155	  it in a component test.
156	- **"Elegir fecha".** A `<button type="button">` after the text box, accessible name
157	  "Elegir fecha: {label}", `LucideCalendarDays` hidden. It is the one new Tab stop (US-04-BR-13).
158	- **Calendar dialog.** Opened with the CDK `Dialog`: `ariaModal: true`, labelled by the visible
159	  month-and-year text (not a heading, US-04-BR-13), `autoFocus` on the day that holds the roving
160	  `tabindex="0"`, focus returned to "Elegir fecha" on close by passing that button as
161	  `restoreFocus` (the CDK default, `restoreFocus = true`, returns to whatever was focused before
162	  opening, verified in `fesm2022/dialog.mjs`; passing the element also covers browsers where a
163	  pointer click does not focus a button), backdrop, `disableAnimations: true`. The CDK dialog marks the siblings of the overlay container `aria-hidden="true"` while
164	  open (`fesm2022/dialog.mjs`, `_hideNonDialogContentFromAssistiveTechnology`) and traps Tab. Wide
165	  screens: a flexible connected position strategy anchored to the date field; below
166	  `--breakpoint-sheet`: the bottom-sheet strategy of §3.
167	- **Grid.** A `<table role="grid">`, columns Monday first with full day names from
168	  `Intl.DateTimeFormat(<country locale tag>, { weekday: 'long' })`, one `role="gridcell"` per day
169	  with `aria-label` "15 de mayo de 1990" (`{ day, month: 'long', year }`; Node 24 ICU gives exactly
170	  "15 de mayo de 1990" and "mayo de 1990" for es-CO and es-CL), `aria-selected` on the stored day,
171	  `aria-disabled="true"` on disabled days (still reachable with arrows, not choosable). Roving
172	  tabindex. Keys go through the pure `nextFocusDate(date, key, shift)`: arrows ±1 day / ±7 days
173	  crossing months, Home/End to Monday/Sunday of the week, PageUp/PageDown ±1 month clamped to the
174	  month's last day, Shift+PageUp/PageDown ±1 year clamped (29/02/2000 → 28/02/2001), Enter/Space
175	  choose, Escape closes. `@angular/aria`'s `ngGrid` is not used: it moves only inside the rendered
176	  rows (arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End in `_widget-chunk.mjs`) and has no PageUp/PageDown, so the
177	  calendar would override most keys anyway.
178	- **Year list.** "Elegir año" swaps the grid for an `ngListbox` (`focusMode="roving"`,
179	  `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`) of the years of `yearRange()`, the current year
180	  selected; Enter chooses, returns to the grid on the same day and month of the chosen year (clamped).
181	- **Disabled days and range (D6).** `isDayDisabled(config, iso, today)` is
182	  `validateField(config, iso, today) !== null` (the value is never empty, so "required" never
183	  applies). `latestValidDate()` probes backwards from today with the same function;
184	  `yearRange()` is [Y−120, year of the latest valid date] when the field has any rule that
185	  disables days, else [Y−120, Y+10] (Q-12). No `minAge` arithmetic is written twice.
186	
187	#### 5. Signal Forms integration (D3)
188	
189	- `CustomSelect` and `DateField` implement `FormValueControl<string>` (`@publicApi 22.0`): a
190	  required `value = model<string>()`, a `touch` output emitted when focus leaves the whole widget
191	  (control, button, panel), and a `focus()` method that focuses the labelled element. The form
192	  template binds them with the existing narrowing accessor `[formField]="text(config.key)"`; no new
193	  cast (ADR-0004's "two accessors are the only casts" holds).
194	- `focusBoundControl()` calls the control's `focus()` when it is implemented (typings of
195	  `FormUiControl.focus`: "If the focus method is not implemented, Signal Forms will attempt to focus
196	  the host element"), so a failed "Continuar" focuses the combobox or the date text box (AC-10 of
197	  US-01, unchanged).
198	- The components declare **no** inputs named `invalid`, `required`, `touched`, `errors` or
199	  `disabled`: `FormField` auto-binds inputs with those names (`FormUiControl`), which would show
200	  `aria-invalid` before the field is touched. The form passes the shown-error state explicitly.
201	- Stored values: option `value`, ISO date or `''`, as before (ADR-0003, ADR-0004).
202	
203	#### 6. Store writer (amends the ADR-0004 implementation note)
204	
205	`date` keys leave the `nativeKeys` set of `quote-form.ts`: the date model now holds `''` for
206	unreadable text, so the model is the truth and `flushModel()` writes date keys like text and select
207	keys. `syncNative` and `validity.badInput` remain for `number` only.

209	#### 7. Lazy step 1 (D8)
210	
211	Measured on a throwaway copy of `frontend/` (production build, `@angular/build` 22.3.0; baseline
212	initial `main` 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer): `@angular/aria` combobox and listbox with CDK
213	overlay, dialog, a11y and layout **+125.40 kB raw / +27.81 kB transfer**; CDK alone **+99.29 /
214	+22.58**. With the icons of ADR-0010, an eager build would pass the 500 kB warning. The
215	`/:country/datos` route therefore uses `loadComponent` for `QuoteFormPage`, so these packages and
216	the step 1 icons load in a lazy chunk. The address, the guards and the "focus the arriving `h1`"
217	rule of ADR-0001 are unchanged; the existing static guard forbids lazy loading only in the summary
218	feature (US-03-AC-03). The budgets of `angular.json` are not changed.
219	
220	#### 8. What tests can and cannot see
221	
222	- **Component tests (jsdom 31.0.1).** jsdom has no `showPopover` and no `inert` (checked in the
223	  installed package), so the CDK falls back to its overlay container under `document.body`: panels
224	  and the calendar render **outside** the component's root. Helpers find them through the
225	  combobox's `aria-controls` (once rendered) or by role in `document`, as spec §11.1 already plans.
226	  The overlay container is torn down between tests.
227	- **E2E (Playwright).** Page-wide role queries are unaffected by where the panel sits. Focus trap,
228	  real key sequences, bottom-sheet geometry and the 44 px boxes are proven here.

230	### Consequences
231	
232	- Good, because the APG combobox wiring comes from a maintained Angular package, not from our code
233	  (D1, D2), and the date logic that is ours is pure and unit-tested row by row.
234	- Good, because the labelled element stays a native `<input>` or `<button>`: `<label for>`,
235	  `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the `aria-*` bindings keep working (D4); §11.1's changes stay
236	  by role and label.
237	- Good, because validation, messages, stored values and the submit focus rule do not change
238	  (D3): `validateField` is still the only rule engine, now also deciding disabled days (D6).
239	- Good, because the bundle stays within budget by moving step 1 to a lazy chunk (D8).
240	- Bad, because `@angular/aria` has been stable only since 22.0.0 (2026-06-03, about five and a half
241	  months) and its combobox was rewritten in that release (legacy combobox removed,
242	  `SimpleCombobox` promoted to `Combobox`, `values` renamed `value`) — mitigation: pinned 22.3.0;
243	  the use is confined to `CustomSelect` and the year list; every keyboard row is a test.
244	- Bad, because `@angular/aria` renders the popup lazily, so `aria-controls` is absent while the
245	  combobox is collapsed, at least until the list has been opened once (host binding `[attr.aria-controls]: _pattern.popupId()`, and the popup
246	  widget registers only when rendered), while WAI-ARIA 1.2 says authors "MUST set aria-controls on a
247	  combobox element to a value that refers to the combobox popup element" — mitigation: the gap is
248	  reported to the spec (*Spec impact* 3) and checked with a screen reader at HC3. `preserveContent`
249	  (an inherited input of `Combobox`) keeps the popup template rendered after the first open, but
250	  the listbox sits inside the CDK overlay's own template, which is detached on close, so the
251	  developer must confirm in a component test whether the reference survives a close; if the human
252	  requires strict conformance, option B can replace `@angular/aria` inside `CustomSelect` without
253	  touching the form.
254	- Bad, because the wrapper still owns several behaviours (Alt+ArrowDown, Tab commit, collapsed
255	  typeahead, Escape restore, filtering, announcements, sheet) — mitigation: each maps to an AC-06/07
256	  row and is tested in both select kinds.
257	- Bad, because the date text needs a custom `format` to keep unreadable text visible (verified
258	  `linkedSignal` hazard) — mitigation: AC-08 rows with an empty `stored` value test exactly this.
259	- Bad, because jsdom cannot show the top layer, `inert` or real focus trapping — mitigation: e2e.
260	- Neutral: two packages of about 3.6 MB (`@angular/cdk`) and 1.2 MB (`@angular/aria`) unpacked in
261	  `node_modules`; only what is imported reaches the bundle.
262	
263	### Strongest argument against
264	
265	Option B (CDK only) builds on the most proven parts of the Angular ecosystem:
266	`ActiveDescendantKeyManager`, `Overlay` and `Dialog` have years of production use, while
267	`@angular/aria` has been stable for under six months, had its combobox rewritten with breaking
268	changes in 22.0.0, has had about two dozen fixes since, leaves `aria-controls` off a collapsed
269	combobox, has no date picker at all, and adds 26 kB raw on top of the CDK. With B every
270	ARIA attribute is ours to set exactly as the APG says, so the `aria-controls` gap does not exist,
271	and there is one primitive library to understand instead of two.
272	
273	**Why we accept it:** under B the combobox's role, states, key relay, typeahead hand-off and
274	close-on-focus-out are hand-written: that is the "from scratch" part the story rules out, and the
275	part where accessibility bugs usually live. `@angular/aria` is the Angular team's implementation of
276	exactly that pattern, its developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0, and it peer-pins the same CDK
277	we need anyway. The decision is contained: `@angular/aria` is used only inside `CustomSelect` and
278	the year list, both behind `FormValueControl<string>`, so falling back to B later rewrites one
279	component, not the form. The 26 kB are in a lazy chunk.

300	## Pros and Cons of the Options
301	
302	### A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk` (chosen)
303	
304	- Good, because the combobox and listbox follow the APG pattern with library-maintained ARIA and
305	  keyboard wiring; works on `<input>` and `<button>`.
306	- Good, because the CDK covers positioning, popover top layer, bottom sheet, modal focus trap and
307	  return, `aria-hidden` of the page behind, and announcements.
308	- Bad, because the library is young (stable since 22.0.0) and has gaps the wrapper fills.
309	- Bad, because +125.40 kB raw for both packages (measured), hence the lazy step 1.
310	
311	### B. `@angular/cdk` only
312	
313	- Good, because every primitive is long-established; one library; full control of every attribute.
314	- Good, because +99.29 kB raw (measured), 26 kB less than A.
315	- Bad, because the combobox ARIA wiring and key handling are hand-written around the key manager:
316	  more custom accessibility code to get right and to test (story: "not from scratch").
317	- Bad, because `cdk/listbox` expects focus inside the listbox, which does not fit a combobox whose
318	  focus stays on the input; only the year list could use it.
319	
320	### C. Angular Material 22.3.0
321	
322	`@angular/material@22.3.0`, MIT (npm view, 2026-11-21). Not measured.
323	
324	- Good, because `mat-datepicker` is a complete, mature date picker with month and multi-year views
325	  and a pluggable date adapter; `mat-autocomplete` covers the search case.
326	- Bad, because `mat-select`'s focus element is the `<mat-select>` host, a custom element that a
327	  `<label for>` cannot target, so `label.control` and the §11.1 helpers break (D4).
328	- Bad, because Material's own theming (system tokens, density, typography) competes with ADR-0010's
329	  token tiers; restyling to the brief means overriding Material's internal structure.
330	- Bad, because it is the heaviest option and adds a third Angular package family to upgrade.

415	  blocker.

# ADR-0012: Accessible custom select and date picker on `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, bound to Signal Forms (amends ADR-0004)

## Context and Problem Statement

US-04 replaces the browser's `<select>` and `<input type="date">` of step 1 with design-system
controls: a select with an icon, search for long lists and the selected option marked, and a date
field that accepts typed dd/mm/aaaa and opens a calendar with month and year navigation and days
disabled by the `minAge` rule (US-04-BR-05, BR-06). The story requires them to be "built on
accessible primitives, not from scratch: Angular CDK (Overlay, Listbox, a11y) or `@angular/aria`
if it is stable in our version", with the WAI-ARIA combobox/listbox and date picker dialog
patterns, a bottom sheet on mobile, and validations and stored values unchanged. ADR-0004
(Accepted) chose Signal Forms with **native controls** (its driver D7) and its implementation note
makes `syncNative` the only writer of number and date keys, built on `validity.badInput`. This ADR
picks the primitives, defines how the controls plug into Signal Forms and the shared validation
core, and amends ADR-0004 where it assumed native controls (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11..Q-13).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. WAI-ARIA APG patterns: combobox with listbox popup (select-only and list autocomplete), date
  picker dialog; full keyboard map of US-04-AC-06, AC-09; focus trapped and returned; polite
  announcements (story; US-04-BR-05, BR-06, BR-13).
- D2. Built on primitives, not from scratch; exact versions, permissive licence; `@angular/cdk`
  equal to the framework version (story; US-04-BR-14; CLAUDE.md §4).
- D3. Same validation, same stored values, same error timing and focus target as before
  (US-04-BR-07, AC-11; ADR-0004: string editing model, `validateField` as the only rule engine,
  `touched && invalid`, `focusBoundControl()` on a failed submit; ADR-0003 stored shape).
- D4. The labelled, focused element is an `<input>` or `<button>` targeted by the field's
  `<label for>`, so `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the existing `aria-*` bindings keep working
  (US-04-BR-05, Q-04 constraint, Q-06, §11.1).
- D5. Typed date dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of the browser locale, stored as ISO;
  unreadable text behaves like the former `badInput` (US-04-BR-06, Q-05; US-01-BR-01, AC-09 note).
- D6. Disabled days come from the same pure validator, no second implementation (US-04-BR-06).
- D7. Panels: popover on wide screens, bottom sheet below 600 px; 44 × 44 px targets; no horizontal
  scroll (US-04-BR-11, AC-12, Q-13).
- D8. Bundle budgets (`angular.json`: initial 500 kB warning) kept or justified (spec §9).
- D9. Testable in jsdom component tests and Playwright e2e by role and label, never by class
  (story; spec §11.1).

## Considered Options

1. **A. `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 for the combobox, listbox and year list, with `@angular/cdk`
   22.3.0** for overlay positioning, the calendar dialog (focus trap and return), live
   announcements and breakpoints; the calendar grid's date navigation as a pure function.
2. **B. `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0 only**: Overlay, `ActiveDescendantKeyManager` (and `cdk/listbox` for
   the year list), `Dialog`, `LiveAnnouncer`; the combobox roles, states and key handling wired by
   hand around the key manager.
3. **C. Angular Material 22.3.0** (`mat-select` / `mat-autocomplete`, `mat-datepicker` with its
   multi-year view), restyled to the design system.

Building the widgets from scratch is excluded by the story.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk`"**, because `@angular/aria` is stable at
22.x (the developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0) and implements the APG combobox wiring that
option B would have us write by hand (role and states, `aria-activedescendant`, key relay,
typeahead, close on focus-out), which is closest to "from scratch" (D1, D2). It works on an
`<input>` (editable) and on a `<button>` (select-only), so the labelled element stays a labelable
native element (D4). The CDK supplies what `@angular/aria` does not have: overlay positioning with
a bottom sheet, a modal dialog with focus trap and return, and the live announcer. Material (C)
would bring a complete date picker but a select host that a `<label for>` cannot target and a
theming system that competes with our token tiers.

### What is decided

#### 1. Packages (new dependencies)

| Package | Version | Licence | Peers (verified) | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `@angular/cdk` | **22.3.0** | MIT | `@angular/core`, `common`, `forms`, `platform-browser` `^22.0.0 \|\| ^23.0.0`; `rxjs ^6.5.3 \|\| ^7.4.0`; deps `tslib`, `parse5` | Overlay, Dialog, a11y (`LiveAnnouncer`), layout (`BreakpointObserver`) |
| `@angular/aria` | **22.3.0** | MIT | `@angular/cdk` **`22.3.0`** (exact), `@angular/core ^22.0.0 \|\| ^23.0.0` | `Combobox`, `ComboboxPopup`, `ComboboxWidget`, `Listbox`, `Option` |

Both equal the framework version; an Angular upgrade (CLAUDE.md §4) moves all `@angular/*`
packages together. Installed with `npm install -E`.

#### 2. Components and pure functions (names per CLAUDE.md §6)

| File | Identifier | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `shared/custom-select.ts` (+ `.html`, `.css`) | `CustomSelect` (`app-custom-select`) | Select-only or searchable combobox, `FormValueControl<string>` |
| `shared/date-field.ts` | `DateField` (`app-date-field`) | Date text box + "Elegir fecha" button, `FormValueControl<string>` |
| `shared/calendar.ts` | `Calendar` (`app-calendar`) | Dialog content: month label, year list, grid, buttons |
| `shared/date-text.ts` | `parseDateText()`, `formatDateText()` | Pure, typed-date grammar of Q-05 |
| `shared/calendar-dates.ts` | `monthGrid()`, `nextFocusDate()`, `isDayDisabled()`, `latestValidDate()`, `yearRange()` | Pure, injectable "today" |
| `shared/select-search.ts` | `filterOptions()`, `normaliseForSearch()`, `SEARCH_THRESHOLD = 4` | Pure, accent- and case-insensitive contains |

#### 3. The custom select

- **Focus element.** Select-only (fewer than `SEARCH_THRESHOLD` options): a
  `<button type="button" ngCombobox>`; `@angular/aria` treats any non-`input`/`textarea` element as
  non-editable (`_combobox-chunk.mjs`: `isEditable` checks the tag), so Enter, Space and ArrowDown
  open it and printable keys are relayed to the list for typeahead. Searchable (at or above the
  threshold): an `<input type="text" ngCombobox>`; typing expands it and writes the filter text.
  Either element gets `id="field-<key>"` (input `controlId`), so the existing `<label for>` targets
  it. Its accessible name is the label; for the button variant `aria-labelledby` also points at the
  label, so the shown value is not folded into the name in any browser.
- **Attributes.** `@angular/aria` binds `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`,
  `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-controls`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-autocomplete` (packed
  `fesm2022/combobox.mjs` host bindings). The form binds `aria-required`, `aria-invalid` and
  `aria-describedby` through inputs of `CustomSelect` exactly as today (ADR-0004: bound
  explicitly), applied to the focus element.
- **List.** `<ul ngComboboxWidget ngListbox>` inside `<ng-template ngComboboxPopup>`, with
  `focusMode="activedescendant"`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`; one `ngOption` per
  configured option in `sortOrder`, `aria-selected` from the listbox; the selected one shows
  `LucideCheck` (hidden) and a style. The prompt "Selecciona una opción" is not an option: it is the
  button's text when the value is `''`, and the input's placeholder for a searchable select.
- **Behaviour owned by `CustomSelect`** (not provided by `@angular/aria`, each tied to a test row):
  Alt+ArrowDown opens on the current option (AC-06); Tab with the list open commits the active
  option and lets focus move (AC-06); on a collapsed select-only, a printable key opens and moves to
  the first match (AC-06); Escape or leaving a searchable select restores the shown label and clears
  the filter without changing the value (AC-07); filtering through `filterOptions()` with the first
  match active (Q-11); the result count or the empty text announced politely through the CDK
  `LiveAnnouncer` (AC-07, §8.1); a pointer click outside closes without changing the value.
- **Panel placement.** A `cdkConnectedOverlay` inside the popup template, anchored to the combobox,
  `cdkConnectedOverlayUsePopover="inline"`: in browsers with the Popover API the panel is a native
  popover in the top layer, inserted next to the trigger (`@angular/cdk@22.3.0`
  `createOverlayRef` defaults `usePopover` to `true` when `showPopover` exists;
  `FlexibleOverlayPopoverLocation` `'inline'` inserts it next to the trigger). Below
  `--breakpoint-sheet` (`BreakpointObserver` with `(min-width: 37.5em)` false) the same panel uses a
  global position strategy anchored to the viewport bottom: full width, at most 85% of the viewport
  height, scrollable list, backdrop, option rows of 48 px, and a "Cerrar" button for touch
  (`tabindex="-1"`, since focus stays on the combobox and Escape or Tab close it for keyboard users).
  Overlays are created with `disableAnimations: true` (ADR-0013).

#### 4. The date field and the calendar

- **Text box.** `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" id="field-<key>">`, placeholder
  "dd/mm/aaaa", hint "Formato: dd/mm/aaaa" first in `aria-describedby`. No input mask.
- **Parsing (pure, `date-text.ts`).** `parseDateText(text)` returns `''` for blank text, the ISO
  `YYYY-MM-DD` for `d/m/yyyy` with `/`, `-` or `.` separators (1–2 digit day and month) or exactly
  8 digits `ddmmyyyy`, and `null` for anything else, including impossible dates (31/04, 29/02 of a
  non-leap year) and 2-digit years (Q-05). `formatDateText(iso)` returns `dd/mm/yyyy`. Every AC-08
  row is a unit test. The function lives next to the validators and imports nothing from Angular.
- **Binding (`transformedValue`).** `DateField` keeps the shown text with Signal Forms'
  `transformedValue(value, { parse, format })` (`@publicApi 22.0`, `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
  typings). `parse` returns `{ value: iso }`, `{ value: '' }` for blank, and
  `{ value: '', error: { kind: 'parse', message: '' } }` for unreadable text, so the stored value
  is `''` and the field is invalid through a `parse` error, which Signal Forms reports to the bound
  field automatically and which the existing `errorOf()` already maps to the US-01-AC-09 message
  rules (no new message). **Verified hazard:** in `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
  (`fesm2022/signals.mjs`, `transformedValue`), the raw value is a `linkedSignal(() =>
  format(value()))`, so writing `''` to the model would recompute the shown text to `''` and erase
  what the person typed (the R1-F03 failure of US-01 in a new form). Therefore `format(iso)` returns
  the last typed text whenever that text parses to `iso` (unreadable text parses to `''`), and
  `formatDateText(iso)` otherwise. On blur a readable text is normalised to dd/mm/aaaa. A calendar
  choice writes the model, and the text follows through `format`. AC-08's empty-`stored` rows prove
  it in a component test.
- **"Elegir fecha".** A `<button type="button">` after the text box, accessible name
  "Elegir fecha: {label}", `LucideCalendarDays` hidden. It is the one new Tab stop (US-04-BR-13).
- **Calendar dialog.** Opened with the CDK `Dialog`: `ariaModal: true`, labelled by the visible
  month-and-year text (not a heading, US-04-BR-13), `autoFocus` on the day that holds the roving
  `tabindex="0"`, focus returned to "Elegir fecha" on close by passing that button as
  `restoreFocus` (the CDK default, `restoreFocus = true`, returns to whatever was focused before
  opening, verified in `fesm2022/dialog.mjs`; passing the element also covers browsers where a
  pointer click does not focus a button), backdrop, `disableAnimations: true`. The CDK dialog marks the siblings of the overlay container `aria-hidden="true"` while
  open (`fesm2022/dialog.mjs`, `_hideNonDialogContentFromAssistiveTechnology`) and traps Tab. Wide
  screens: a flexible connected position strategy anchored to the date field; below
  `--breakpoint-sheet`: the bottom-sheet strategy of §3.
- **Grid.** A `<table role="grid">`, columns Monday first with full day names from
  `Intl.DateTimeFormat(<country locale tag>, { weekday: 'long' })`, one `role="gridcell"` per day
  with `aria-label` "15 de mayo de 1990" (`{ day, month: 'long', year }`; Node 24 ICU gives exactly
  "15 de mayo de 1990" and "mayo de 1990" for es-CO and es-CL), `aria-selected` on the stored day,
  `aria-disabled="true"` on disabled days (still reachable with arrows, not choosable). Roving
  tabindex. Keys go through the pure `nextFocusDate(date, key, shift)`: arrows ±1 day / ±7 days
  crossing months, Home/End to Monday/Sunday of the week, PageUp/PageDown ±1 month clamped to the
  month's last day, Shift+PageUp/PageDown ±1 year clamped (29/02/2000 → 28/02/2001), Enter/Space
  choose, Escape closes. `@angular/aria`'s `ngGrid` is not used: it moves only inside the rendered
  rows (arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End in `_widget-chunk.mjs`) and has no PageUp/PageDown, so the
  calendar would override most keys anyway.
- **Year list.** "Elegir año" swaps the grid for an `ngListbox` (`focusMode="roving"`,
  `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`) of the years of `yearRange()`, the current year
  selected; Enter chooses, returns to the grid on the same day and month of the chosen year (clamped).
- **Disabled days and range (D6).** `isDayDisabled(config, iso, today)` is
  `validateField(config, iso, today) !== null` (the value is never empty, so "required" never
  applies). `latestValidDate()` probes backwards from today with the same function;
  `yearRange()` is [Y−120, year of the latest valid date] when the field has any rule that
  disables days, else [Y−120, Y+10] (Q-12). No `minAge` arithmetic is written twice.

#### 5. Signal Forms integration (D3)

- `CustomSelect` and `DateField` implement `FormValueControl<string>` (`@publicApi 22.0`): a
  required `value = model<string>()`, a `touch` output emitted when focus leaves the whole widget
  (control, button, panel), and a `focus()` method that focuses the labelled element. The form
  template binds them with the existing narrowing accessor `[formField]="text(config.key)"`; no new
  cast (ADR-0004's "two accessors are the only casts" holds).
- `focusBoundControl()` calls the control's `focus()` when it is implemented (typings of
  `FormUiControl.focus`: "If the focus method is not implemented, Signal Forms will attempt to focus
  the host element"), so a failed "Continuar" focuses the combobox or the date text box (AC-10 of
  US-01, unchanged).
- The components declare **no** inputs named `invalid`, `required`, `touched`, `errors` or
  `disabled`: `FormField` auto-binds inputs with those names (`FormUiControl`), which would show
  `aria-invalid` before the field is touched. The form passes the shown-error state explicitly.
- Stored values: option `value`, ISO date or `''`, as before (ADR-0003, ADR-0004).

#### 6. Store writer (amends the ADR-0004 implementation note)

`date` keys leave the `nativeKeys` set of `quote-form.ts`: the date model now holds `''` for
unreadable text, so the model is the truth and `flushModel()` writes date keys like text and select
keys. `syncNative` and `validity.badInput` remain for `number` only.

#### 7. Lazy step 1 (D8)

Measured on a throwaway copy of `frontend/` (production build, `@angular/build` 22.3.0; baseline
initial `main` 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer): `@angular/aria` combobox and listbox with CDK
overlay, dialog, a11y and layout **+125.40 kB raw / +27.81 kB transfer**; CDK alone **+99.29 /
+22.58**. With the icons of ADR-0010, an eager build would pass the 500 kB warning. The
`/:country/datos` route therefore uses `loadComponent` for `QuoteFormPage`, so these packages and
the step 1 icons load in a lazy chunk. The address, the guards and the "focus the arriving `h1`"
rule of ADR-0001 are unchanged; the existing static guard forbids lazy loading only in the summary
feature (US-03-AC-03). The budgets of `angular.json` are not changed.

#### 8. What tests can and cannot see

- **Component tests (jsdom 31.0.1).** jsdom has no `showPopover` and no `inert` (checked in the
  installed package), so the CDK falls back to its overlay container under `document.body`: panels
  and the calendar render **outside** the component's root. Helpers find them through the
  combobox's `aria-controls` (once rendered) or by role in `document`, as spec §11.1 already plans.
  The overlay container is torn down between tests.
- **E2E (Playwright).** Page-wide role queries are unaffected by where the panel sits. Focus trap,
  real key sequences, bottom-sheet geometry and the 44 px boxes are proven here.

### Consequences

- Good, because the APG combobox wiring comes from a maintained Angular package, not from our code
  (D1, D2), and the date logic that is ours is pure and unit-tested row by row.
- Good, because the labelled element stays a native `<input>` or `<button>`: `<label for>`,
  `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the `aria-*` bindings keep working (D4); §11.1's changes stay
  by role and label.
- Good, because validation, messages, stored values and the submit focus rule do not change
  (D3): `validateField` is still the only rule engine, now also deciding disabled days (D6).
- Good, because the bundle stays within budget by moving step 1 to a lazy chunk (D8).
- Bad, because `@angular/aria` has been stable only since 22.0.0 (2026-06-03, about five and a half
  months) and its combobox was rewritten in that release (legacy combobox removed,
  `SimpleCombobox` promoted to `Combobox`, `values` renamed `value`) — mitigation: pinned 22.3.0;
  the use is confined to `CustomSelect` and the year list; every keyboard row is a test.
- Bad, because `@angular/aria` renders the popup lazily, so `aria-controls` is absent while the
  combobox is collapsed, at least until the list has been opened once (host binding `[attr.aria-controls]: _pattern.popupId()`, and the popup
  widget registers only when rendered), while WAI-ARIA 1.2 says authors "MUST set aria-controls on a
  combobox element to a value that refers to the combobox popup element" — mitigation: the gap is
  reported to the spec (*Spec impact* 3) and checked with a screen reader at HC3. `preserveContent`
  (an inherited input of `Combobox`) keeps the popup template rendered after the first open, but
  the listbox sits inside the CDK overlay's own template, which is detached on close, so the
  developer must confirm in a component test whether the reference survives a close; if the human
  requires strict conformance, option B can replace `@angular/aria` inside `CustomSelect` without
  touching the form.
- Bad, because the wrapper still owns several behaviours (Alt+ArrowDown, Tab commit, collapsed
  typeahead, Escape restore, filtering, announcements, sheet) — mitigation: each maps to an AC-06/07
  row and is tested in both select kinds.
- Bad, because the date text needs a custom `format` to keep unreadable text visible (verified
  `linkedSignal` hazard) — mitigation: AC-08 rows with an empty `stored` value test exactly this.
- Bad, because jsdom cannot show the top layer, `inert` or real focus trapping — mitigation: e2e.
- Neutral: two packages of about 3.6 MB (`@angular/cdk`) and 1.2 MB (`@angular/aria`) unpacked in
  `node_modules`; only what is imported reaches the bundle.

### Strongest argument against

Option B (CDK only) builds on the most proven parts of the Angular ecosystem:
`ActiveDescendantKeyManager`, `Overlay` and `Dialog` have years of production use, while
`@angular/aria` has been stable for under six months, had its combobox rewritten with breaking
changes in 22.0.0, has had about two dozen fixes since, leaves `aria-controls` off a collapsed
combobox, has no date picker at all, and adds 26 kB raw on top of the CDK. With B every
ARIA attribute is ours to set exactly as the APG says, so the `aria-controls` gap does not exist,
and there is one primitive library to understand instead of two.

**Why we accept it:** under B the combobox's role, states, key relay, typeahead hand-off and
close-on-focus-out are hand-written: that is the "from scratch" part the story rules out, and the
part where accessibility bugs usually live. `@angular/aria` is the Angular team's implementation of
exactly that pattern, its developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0, and it peer-pins the same CDK
we need anyway. The decision is contained: `@angular/aria` is used only inside `CustomSelect` and
the year list, both behind `FormValueControl<string>`, so falling back to B later rewrites one
component, not the form. The 26 kB are in a lazy chunk.

### Confirmation

- Unit tests: `date-text.spec.ts` (every AC-08 row), `calendar-dates.spec.ts` (every AC-09 keyboard
  row through `nextFocusDate`, every AC-10 row with a pinned clock, year ranges of AC-10),
  `select-search.spec.ts` (AC-07 filters, accents, case).
- Component tests: `custom-select.spec.ts` (AC-05, every AC-06 row on "Marca" and on "Tipo de
  documento", AC-07, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-selected`, prompt),
  `date-field.spec.ts` (AC-08 including the rows with empty `stored` and text kept, hydration,
  AC-09 flow and names, AC-10), `quote-form-page.spec.ts` per §11.1 (failed "Continuar" focuses the
  combobox and the date text box through `focusBoundControl()`).
- E2E `us-04-design-system.spec.ts`: real keyboard on select and calendar, focus trap and return,
  panels at three viewports (AC-12), stored object of AC-11.
- Static checks (code-reviewer): `frontend/package.json` pins `@angular/cdk` and `@angular/aria` to
  `22.3.0`; `@angular/aria` is imported only by `custom-select.ts` and `calendar.ts`; no
  `ReactiveFormsModule`/`FormControl` (ADR-0004 grep unchanged); the only `as unknown as FieldTree`
  casts are still the two accessors; `field-validators.ts`, `date-text.ts` and `calendar-dates.ts`
  import nothing from `@angular/*`.
- HC3: screen reader pass on the select (both kinds), the calendar and the year list (spec §9).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk` (chosen)

- Good, because the combobox and listbox follow the APG pattern with library-maintained ARIA and
  keyboard wiring; works on `<input>` and `<button>`.
- Good, because the CDK covers positioning, popover top layer, bottom sheet, modal focus trap and
  return, `aria-hidden` of the page behind, and announcements.
- Bad, because the library is young (stable since 22.0.0) and has gaps the wrapper fills.
- Bad, because +125.40 kB raw for both packages (measured), hence the lazy step 1.

### B. `@angular/cdk` only

- Good, because every primitive is long-established; one library; full control of every attribute.
- Good, because +99.29 kB raw (measured), 26 kB less than A.
- Bad, because the combobox ARIA wiring and key handling are hand-written around the key manager:
  more custom accessibility code to get right and to test (story: "not from scratch").
- Bad, because `cdk/listbox` expects focus inside the listbox, which does not fit a combobox whose
  focus stays on the input; only the year list could use it.

### C. Angular Material 22.3.0

`@angular/material@22.3.0`, MIT (npm view, 2026-11-21). Not measured.

- Good, because `mat-datepicker` is a complete, mature date picker with month and multi-year views
  and a pluggable date adapter; `mat-autocomplete` covers the search case.
- Bad, because `mat-select`'s focus element is the `<mat-select>` host, a custom element that a
  `<label for>` cannot target, so `label.control` and the §11.1 helpers break (D4).
- Bad, because Material's own theming (system tokens, density, typography) competes with ADR-0010's
  token tiers; restyling to the brief means overriding Material's internal structure.
- Bad, because it is the heaviest option and adds a third Angular package family to upgrade.

## Amendments to accepted ADRs (explicit; the accepted files are not edited)

**ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20):

1. Driver **D7** "Native controls, accessible name, description, required and invalid states, error
   announced once" now reads, for `select` and `date` fields only: custom controls built on
   `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, whose labelled element is a native `<input>` or `<button>`
   targeted by the field's `<label for>`, with the same accessible name, description, required and
   invalid bindings and the same one-time error announcement. `text`, `number` and `checkbox` stay
   native.
2. The **implementation note** (`adr/README.md`, ADR-0004 row): "`syncNative` is the only writer of
   number and date keys" becomes "of number keys"; date keys are written by `flushModel()` from the
   model, which holds `''` for unreadable text through `transformedValue` (§4, §6). The submit gate,
   `onInvalid` with `focusBoundControl()`, and the `parse`-error message rule are unchanged.

If this ADR is accepted, the `adr/README.md` row of ADR-0004 reads "Accepted (amended by ADR-0012)",
and the implementation-notes table gets a pointer row.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. **§11.1, AC-05 and `expectEmptyStep1`**: for a **searchable** select (an `<input>`), the prompt
   "Selecciona una opción" is the placeholder, so `inputValue()` is `''` when empty. Tests of the
   empty state should assert the placeholder (or the accessible description) plus the stored value,
   not `inputValue() === 'Selecciona una opción'`. For a select-only (a `<button>`), the prompt is
   the visible text.
2. **US-04-AC-09** "the page behind is inert": the CDK dialog gives a focus trap, a backdrop that
   takes pointer events and `aria-hidden="true"` on the page behind, not the HTML `inert`
   attribute. The scenario should assert those three (or the developer adds `inert` and the test
   checks it in e2e; jsdom has no `inert`).
3. **§11.1 `quote-form-page.spec.ts` "select → role=combobox with `aria-expanded="false"` and
   `aria-controls`"**: with `@angular/aria`, `aria-controls` is bound only while the list is
   rendered; while collapsed it is absent (at least before the first open). Either relax that
   assertion to "while expanded" or accept option B for `CustomSelect`.
4. **US-04-Q-12 / AC-09 "Monday first"**: CLDR week data (Node 24 ICU, `Intl.Locale.weekInfo`)
   gives Sunday as the first day for `es-CO` and Monday for `es-CL`. The spec fixes Monday for both
   countries; the human should confirm this is intended for Colombia.
5. **US-04-Q-11 with Q-13 on phones**: a searchable select on a 360 px screen opens a bottom sheet
   while the on-screen keyboard is up; the sheet must fit above the keyboard. The ADR keeps one
   combobox pattern at every width (focus stays in the text box); the HC3 phone pass must check
   this, and if it fails, the fallback is a sheet with its own search box (a dialog), which changes
   the ARIA pattern on narrow screens and needs a spec change.
6. **US-01 supersessions** listed in US-04-Q-04 (Q-22 native date, §9 native controls, BR-02 prompt
   as an option) are consistent with this ADR.

## More Information

- **Verified on 2026-11-21** (npm registry, `npm pack` into a temporary directory, installed
  packages in `frontend/node_modules`, and a throwaway build; nothing installed in the project):
  - `npm view @angular/aria@22.3.0`: MIT; peers `@angular/cdk 22.3.0`, `@angular/core ^22.0.0 || ^23.0.0`;
    published 2026-11-18. Entry points: `accordion`, `combobox`, `grid`, `listbox`, `menu`, `tabs`,
    `toolbar`, `tree` (each with `testing`); no date picker.
  - `npm view @angular/cdk@22.3.0`: MIT; peers as in §1; deps `tslib`, `parse5`.
  - Stability: angular/components `CHANGELOG.md`, release **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**: "remove developer
    preview tag from aria" (#33232) and "promote simple-combobox to stable un-prefixed combobox";
    breaking: "The legacy combobox and autocomplete implementations have been removed", "Renames the
    values input/model to value in Combobox, Listbox, …". About 24 entries in the `aria` scope from
    22.0.1 to 22.3.0 (counted from a summarised read of the CHANGELOG; approximate). The packed
    typings carry no stability tags. angular.dev "Angular Aria" overview (site built at v22.3.0):
    no stability notice, a "New" label; patterns listed: Autocomplete, Listbox, Select,
    Multiselect, Combobox, Menu, Menubar, Toolbar, Accordion, Tabs, Tree, Grid.
  - API facts from packed `@angular/aria@22.3.0`: `Combobox` inputs `disabled`, `readonly`,
    `softDisabled`, `alwaysExpanded`, `tabindex`, models `expanded`, `value`; `ComboboxPopup`
    `popupType` `'listbox' | 'tree' | 'grid' | 'dialog'`; `Listbox` inputs `wrap`, `focusMode`
    (`activedescendant` | `roving`), `selectionMode` (`explicit` | `follow`), `typeaheadDelay`,
    model `value`; `DeferredContentAware.preserveContent`.
  - `@angular/forms@22.3.0`: `FormValueControl`, `FormUiControl` (`touch`, `focus()`),
    `transformedValue` and `TransformedValueSignal` are `@publicApi 22.0`; `transformedValue` builds
    the raw value with `linkedSignal` (`fesm2022/signals.mjs`).
  - jsdom 31.0.1 (`frontend/node_modules/jsdom`): no `showPopover`, no `inert` implementation.
  - WAI-ARIA 1.2, combobox role (w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2, read 2026-11-21): required states and
    properties `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded`.
  - Build measurements: see §7.
- **Third-party skill conflict (CLAUDE.md §1, §5):** the vendored `angular-aria.md` says "Never use
  native HTML elements like `<select>`" and shows `[formField]` bound directly to `ngCombobox`. We
  reach `@angular/aria` on our own drivers, but we do **not** bind `[formField]` to `ngCombobox`:
  its `value` model is the input's text (the search string), not the option value, so it would
  store labels or filter text. The form binds `CustomSelect`, which maps the listbox selection to
  the option value.
- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0004 (amended here), ADR-0003 (stored values unchanged), ADR-0001 (route
  address unchanged; step 1 lazy), ADR-0010 (tokens, icons, breakpoints), ADR-0013 (panel motion,
  `disableAnimations`).
- **Revisit when:** `@angular/aria` ships a date picker or changes its combobox API; the HC3 screen
  reader or phone pass fails on the select or the calendar; the `aria-controls` gap is judged a
  blocker.

- Good, because one page is ever in the DOM (D2), and focus and announcements are untouched (D6).
- Bad, because the old page disappears without an exit animation, so the change is a cut followed by
  a fade-in, less fluid than a cross-fade — mitigation: the fade is short (200 ms) and the step
  indicator fill gives continuity; B can be added later as an enhancement if the human wants a
  cross-fade (see *Revisit*).
- Bad, because closing a panel inside a CDK overlay may not run `animate.leave` (the overlay detaches
  its content) — mitigation: panels close instantly unless the developer proves the leave runs; no
  AC requires a close animation.
- Bad, because writing every animation inside a media block is a discipline — mitigation: the guard
  fails the gate otherwise.
- Neutral: the first page load also plays `page-enter` once; that is the single page-load moment.

### Strongest argument against

The View Transitions route (B) gives a real two-state transition with one line,
`withViewTransitions()`: the browser snapshots the old page and cross-fades it into the new one,
while the live DOM still holds only the new page (so AC-14 holds too). It can even morph the step
indicator between steps with a `view-transition-name`, which is the "animated step indicator" the
story asks for, and browsers without support simply skip it. Enter-only CSS is a hard cut followed
by a fade, the kind of generic "fade-and-rise" the `frontend-design` skill calls a tell of generated
pages.

**Why we accept it:** B only animates route changes, so the panels, errors, skeletons, cards,
spinner and confirmation still need A: two mechanisms, two reduced-motion paths (B also needs
`skipTransition()` or `::view-transition-*` rules under `reduce`, and its pseudo-element
animations show up in `document.getAnimations()` during AC-17). `withViewTransitions` is tagged
`@publicApi 22.3` in the 22.3.0 typings, so it has been public API only since the release we pin,
three days before this ADR. The fade-in here is brief and paired with the indicator fill, and the
one orchestrated moment is the confirmation, as the skill advises. B stays a contained later
enhancement on top of A.

### Confirmation

- Static guard rules of §4 (US-04-AC-17, AC-01).
- E2E `us-04-design-system.spec.ts`: AC-14 and AC-17 as in §4.
- Component tests (AC-15): skeletons are `aria-hidden`, the loading text stays in its live region.
- HC3: the human checks the motion with the OS setting on and off (AC-23).
- `frontend/package.json` contains no `motion`, `gsap`, `@angular/animations` or other animation
  dependency (dependency list guard of ADR-0010).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

| ADR | Title | Status | Date | Stories |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) | Multi-country content strategy and country context (includes wizard routes and step guards) | Accepted (amended by ADR-0006 and ADR-0011) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0002](0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) | Strapi access and security model | Accepted (amended by ADR-0005) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0003](0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) | Front-end persistence of the wizard state | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |

| [0006](0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) | Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01, US-02 |
| [0007](0007-simulated-price-rule.md) | Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function | Accepted (option A, chosen by the human at HC2, 2026-11-21) | 2026-11-21 | US-02, US-03 |
| [0008](0008-simulated-payment.md) | Simulated payment: a visible outcome choice, a front-end gateway boundary, no card data | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |
| [0009](0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) | Terms rich text: Strapi `blocks` rendered by a whitelist component through template bindings | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |

| [0011](0011-country-visuals-amends-adr-0001.md) | Country visuals (flag and accent) as a presentation-only front-end map (amends ADR-0001) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0012](0012-accessible-select-and-date-picker.md) | Accessible custom select and date picker on `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, bound to Signal Forms (amends ADR-0004) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0013](0013-motion-and-reduced-motion.md) | Motion with native `animate.enter` and CSS on duration tokens, enter-only step transition, reduced motion by construction | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |

### Implementation notes on accepted ADRs (no decision change)

Accepted ADRs are not rewritten. When the implementation of an accepted decision changes in a way
that leaves the decision intact, the note goes here.

| ADR | Note | Since |
|---|---|---|
| 0002 | The published-only rule (ADR-0002 calls it a "global middleware") is a **route middleware** on `find`/`findOne`, attached per router through `publishedOnlyConfig()`, so that it runs after Strapi authentication. The decision (no drafts for any unauthenticated read) is unchanged. A backend test guards that every content router uses it. | c3bdb56, 345a016 (US-01-R1-F01); US-01-R2-F06 |
| 0001 | **Summary route registered by US-02 (US-02-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** The route table row `/:country/resumen` keeps its address and its kind of guard; only *who builds it, and when* moves forward. US-02 registers `/:country/resumen` with **no component** (`children: []`, the same pattern ADR-0001 used for `/:country/planes` in US-01) and a `CanActivateFn` step 3 guard, defined in US-02 spec (US-02-AC-15): no valid step 1 for the route's country → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/datos`; no chosen plan, or a stored plan key that is not an offered plan of this page load → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/planes`; both with `replaceUrl: true`. US-03 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard, and may extend the guard only through its own spec. No new decision: ADR-0001 fixed the addresses, the per-step guards, the `RedirectCommand`/`replaceUrl` mechanics and the "earlier story registers the route, later story attaches the page" pattern; it left the guard's content to a story spec. | US-02 spec v0.1 (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15) |
| 0002 | **Terms content-type name (US-03-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** ADR-0002 names the US-03 permission `api::terms.terms.find`. Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a content type whose singular and plural names are equal (`@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/loaders/apis.js:44-62`, `validateContentTypesUnicity`: "The plural name … should be unique"), so the type is **`api::term.term`** (singularName `term`, pluralName `terms`, as in CLAUDE.md §6). Consequently: the public permission is **`api::term.term.find`** (no `findOne`), reconciled in bootstrap with the existing three; the router is `createCoreRouter('api::term.term', publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object (US-01-R2-F03), so `backend/tests/published-only-routes.test.ts` covers it; the REST path stays **`/api/terms`**, which must be added to the GET-only allow-list in `frontend/nginx/default.conf.template` (today `countries|form-fields|plans`). The decision (public `find` only, published-only reads, GET-only proxy, no write token in the browser) is unchanged. | US-03 spec v0.1 (US-03-Q-03, §7.4) |
| 0004 | The submit gate is Signal Forms validity, as decided: `submission.action` runs only for a valid form, and `onInvalid` focuses the first invalid field in `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`. A native `number`/`date` input the browser cannot read gets a Signal Forms `parse` error, and its control model is deliberately left unwritten (writing `''` would erase the visible text). The store therefore follows the control: `syncNative` is the only writer of number and date keys (`''` on `validity.badInput`), and `flushModel()` writes the other types before `completeStep1` (keyboard Enter). 40606e2 had moved the gate to the store with `ignoreValidators: 'all'`, which broke the AC-24 keyboard submit (patched in e92e2c7) and let an emptied date through (US-01-R3-F01). The human chose to restore the Signal Forms gate in eeb23e6. | e92e2c7, eeb23e6 (US-01-R3-F01, R3-F05); US-01-R3-F02 |
| 0003 | **An empty wizard state is represented by no `quote-wizard` entry (US-03-R1-F02).** A state with no step 1 values and no chosen plan leaves no entry in `sessionStorage`. a3f186c added this to `QuoteStore.persist()` as an early `return`, which only skipped the write: an entry that already existed stayed, for example after `prune()` drops every stored key because none is configured any more, so the values of removed fields remained in the tab. b3fdd45 (US-03-R1-F02) fixed it: for an empty state, `persist()` (`frontend/src/app/core/quote-store.ts:163-178`, empty branch `:169-172`) now **removes** any existing entry by calling `clearStorage()` (call on `:170`, method `:180-186`) and then returns, so the invariant "empty state ⇒ no entry" holds in every case, and ADR-0003's "the pruned state is written back" is met by removal when the pruned state is empty (`prune()`, `:88-98`). Consequences: entering a country with an empty step 1 (`enterCountry`, `:42-51`) no longer writes `{country, step1: {values: {}}}`, a change to US-01 behaviour; nothing is lost, because the country is always known from the `/:country` route, which calls `enterCountry` on each entry (ADR-0001), and the entry is written on the first value or plan choice. After a successful payment, `clearQuote()` (`:58-64`) removes the entry, and a reload, a back action or "Nueva cotización" re-enters the country with an empty state, so no entry is found (US-03-AC-11). The decision of ADR-0003 (one versioned `sessionStorage` entry per tab, scoped to one country, cleared on country change and on successful payment) is unchanged. | a3f186c; b3fdd45 (US-03-R1-F02) |
| 0012 | **First day of the calendar week comes from the locale (human decision at HC1, 2026-11-21; spec v0.2, ece558e: US-04-BR-06, US-04-AC-09).** ADR-0012 §4 says "columns Monday first" and "Home/End to Monday/Sunday of the week". Instead, the grid's first column is the first day of the week of the current country's locale tag (Strapi `country`, ADR-0001/ADR-0006) from CLDR through `Intl`: Sunday for `es-CO`, Monday for `es-CL`. Home and End move to the first and last day of that locale's week. The date picker holds no country code and no per-country table: it receives the locale tag and derives the day. **How:** `new Intl.Locale(tag).getWeekInfo().firstDay` (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday). If the method is missing, use the older `weekInfo` accessor. If neither exists, fall back to **Monday** (CLDR's world default, `und-001`). This is a pure function next to `calendar-dates.ts`, with the clock and locale injectable. **Runtime support:** MDN browser-compat-data gives `getWeekInfo` in Chrome 130, Firefox 153, Safari 17 and Node 24.0.0, and the `weekInfo` accessor in Chrome 99 and Safari 15.4 (removed in Safari Technology Preview). Measured on 2026-11-21: Playwright's Chromium 159.0.8154.6 (the only e2e project) has `getWeekInfo` and no longer has `weekInfo`, giving `es-CO` 7 and `es-CL` 1; Node 24.22.1 (Vitest) has both, with the same values; `und-001` gives 1. Firefox and WebKit are not installed for Playwright and were not run. **Fallback effect:** on browsers with neither API (Firefox before 153, Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 99), Colombia shows Monday first. `@angular/common`'s `getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek` is not used: it is `@deprecated 18.0` in 22.3.0 ("Angular recommends relying on the `Intl` API"), and it needs `registerLocaleData` for `es-CO`/`es-CL`, which the app does not register. The rest of ADR-0012 (primitives, binding, keyboard keys, disabled days) is unchanged. | Spec v0.2 (ece558e); HC1 2026-11-21 |

## Backlog (decisions known to be needed)

Numbers are assigned when an ADR is written; this order is only provisional.

| Topic | Why it needs an ADR | Input |
|---|---|---|
| — | No pending ADR for US-01, US-02 or US-03 | — |

Proposed on 2026-11-21 for US-04 (written in parallel with HC1 at the human's request; awaiting
HC2): ADR-0010 (US-04-Q-01, Q-03, Q-08, Q-09, Q-10), ADR-0011 (US-04-Q-02; amends ADR-0001 if
accepted), ADR-0012 (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11..Q-13; amends ADR-0004 if accepted) and ADR-0013
(US-04-Q-14, Q-16). The index rows of ADR-0001 and ADR-0004 change to "amended by" only when the
amending ADR is accepted.

Covered since 2026-11-21 for US-03 (both Accepted at HC2 by the human, 2026-11-21): the simulated
payment (ADR-0008; US-03-Q-01) and the terms rich-text format and rendering (ADR-0009;
US-03-Q-02). The terms content-type name (US-03-Q-03) is an implementation note on ADR-0002 above.

Covered since 2026-11-21: the simulated price rule of US-02 (ADR-0007, Accepted: option A; US-02-Q-01) and
the summary route registered by US-02 (implementation note on ADR-0001 above; US-02-Q-03).

Covered since 2026-11-20: the multi-country content strategy (ADR-0001, which also folds in the
wizard routing and step guards candidate from US-01 spec §10), the Strapi access and security
model (ADR-0002), the front-end persistence of the wizard state (ADR-0003), and the forms library
(ADR-0004, informed by [SPIKE-01](../docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md)).
